leads.notes: THE FACT THAT SHAPED THE RUN: ANHC already runs an ambient AI documentation tool in clinical production, ahead of every Alaska FQHC peer checked. They are not behind and not AI novices, and any future touch that implies either is factually wrong. Patient-majority board meets monthly, so decision latency runs in months and urgency reads badly to that governance. Fiscal year ends June 30th, not September 30th. Draft of record r107419310266212095, nothing superseded. study-critic shipped on round 5, lead-critic on round 1.

leads.segment: Other labor-scarce or paperwork-heavy Alaska SMBs
leads.why_picked: Highest and unshared fit total of 23 page-verified candidates across four segments. Only candidate scoring 5 on reachability, which is the criterion that most often sinks a strong lead at Phase 2. Employee-owned Alaska engineering and surveying firm, 100+ staff, four offices, nearly 95 percent public-client work, CMMC Level 2 certified.
leads.outcome: Declined to sell them the obvious build. The loudest cited pain is proposal work sitting on senior billable seats, carried verbatim on two senior postings in two departments plus a third. We do not sell it, because they hired a Proposal Manager 24 days before the run and because the industry read found no named firm at any size attached to a measured proposal-productivity number with a stated method. The recommendation is the one place in the industry with an independent measurement.
leads.recommended_build: The documentation gap check, Phase 1 of an eventual field record copilot. Rules only, ZERO AI. Before each pay estimate and at closeout it reads the documentation they already produce and reports the contract-required items it did not find, plus everything it could not examine. It never asserts completeness.
leads.roi_summary: 12,000 fixed fee, Phase 1 only, split 4,000 at Gate A and 8,000 at Gate B. RESIZED DOWN FROM 18,000 mid-run after roi_math showed the conservative case recovered only 97 percent and never paid back. At 12,000 the conservative case recovers 119 percent and pays back month 47, most likely 384 percent and month 15. Two sensitivities printed: one person doing both roles drops it to 99 percent and no payback; a fifth overrun on run cost drops it to 109 percent and month 53.
